title: Skin, Sun & Infections
whatItIs: Cement, paints, solvents, resins and oils can cause dermatitis. Outdoor work brings sun damage and skin cancer. Rats, sewage, old water systems and needles can spread infections.
keyFacts: Wet cement is highly alkaline: trapped against the skin, it can quickly cause a serious burn or ulcer.
Dermatitis can be irritant or allergic. Once you're sensitised, any future contact can set it off.
Wash cement or other products off your skin as soon as possible, and wash at breaks and after work.
In the sun: keep your top on, wear a hat with a neck flap, use SPF30 or more and check moles for changes.
Weil's disease comes from rat urine getting into cuts or the eyes, mouth or throat. It starts like flu.
Cover cuts with waterproof dressings, and wash your hands before eating, drinking or smoking.

items.title: Sun (UV)

items.title: Needles
items.text: Treat all as infected. Use tongs and a sharps box.

a.label: Irritant dermatitis
points: Caused by contact with an irritant

b.label: Allergic dermatitis
points: An allergy that can start after weeks, months or years of use
Once you have it, any future contact causes a reaction

onTheTest.question: How do people usually catch Weil's disease (leptospirosis) at work?
options: From rat urine getting into cuts, eyes or mouth
onTheTest.why: HSE: it comes from infected rat urine, entering through cuts or the lining of the mouth, throat and eyes.

onTheTest.question: Wet concrete has got inside your boot. What is the main risk?
options: A chemical burn, as wet cement is highly alkaline
onTheTest.why: HSE: wet cement is highly alkaline; trapped against skin it can quickly cause a serious burn or ulcer.

traps: A tan isn't healthy: it's a sign that UV has damaged your skin.
Years of using cement without trouble don't make you safe: allergy can develop.
Never use solvents to clean paint or grease off your skin.
Gloves only help if no cement or chemical gets inside them.
